titleEn: Need to Pee? Go Right Away!

pages.text: Bang! The bathroom door beside the classroom closed by itself. Timid Lala hunched at the sound. "The wind closed it," said Teacher Bau, opening it again.
Playtime. Lala wanted to finish playing house, but had needed to pee for a while. Those knees kept pressing together. Lala glanced toward the bathroom door.
Bang, the door closed again. Lala covered both ears, afraid of being trapped if it shut. "I will not go." Lala gripped the toy pot tighter.
Their tummy hurt in little jabs. Lala clutched it and twisted about. Careless Duri noticed. "Lala, your face is white!" Lala stamped their feet.
Teacher Bau opened the bathroom door wide and sat outside. "My foot is here. Can you see it through the gap? Need to pee? Go right away!" Lala peeped: a big foot really was there.
Lala repeated softly, "Need to pee? Go right away." Then one foot stepped inside. Teacher Bau's foot was still visible beyond the door.
Lala peed alone. Seeing the foot all the time made it less scary. "Finished!" Lala washed both hands, pushed the door, and came out.
Without a word, Teacher Bau opened the door wide against the wall, then gave Lala one nod. Lala nodded once too.

Now the sound of a closing door did not scare Lala. "One, say right away when I need to go! Two, leave the door wide open! Three, wash hands and come out!" During playtime, Lala went to the bathroom first.

Teacher Bau held Lala's hand and led the way back to the play area. Going right away, instead of holding it, meant no tummyache and no missed play. Handing Duri the pot, Lala said, "Need to pee? Go right away!"
